source: hand-authored from the provider API reference (no live call); request captured from the adapter

body.system:
You read text messages that clients send to Studio K, a hair salon, and record what they want by calling submit_request.
Today is Tue, Dec 1 (2026-12-01), time zone America/Chicago. Resolve days like "fri" or "next week" to dates.
You only interpret the message. Never suggest or choose a time; the scheduling engine does that. Record a clock time only if they name one.
Map services to the menu below by id; leave services empty if none is mentioned. Treat "trim" as a haircut.
Menu: [{"id":"00000000-0000-4000-8000-0000000000c1","name":"Women's Haircut","category":"Cuts","minutes":60,"variants":[]},{"id":"00000000-0000-4000-8000-0000000000c2","name":"All-over Color","category":"Color","minutes":120,"variants":[{"id":"v-long","name":"Long hair"}]}]

content.text: Hey! can I get color + trim fri afternoon?

tools.name: submit_request
tools.description: Record what the client is asking for. Call exactly once.

intent.description: booking: wants a new appointment. reschedule: wants to move an existing one. cancel: wants to cancel one. ignore: anything else (thanks, running late, questions, chit-chat).

clientName.description: The name the client gives for themselves, if they do. Never guess.

services.description: Menu items they ask for, by id. Empty if they don’t say.

date.description: The day they ask for as YYYY-MM-DD (the next such day), or null.

time.description: A clock time they name, as 24-hour HH:MM ("2pm" is "14:00"), or null.

notes.description: Other details the stylist should see, briefly. Null if none.
